answers.answerContent: I can see the Buddha starving himself with the side too extreme in meditation in hopes of enlightenment.
The Buddha only ate the leaves that fell from the tree and touched him. He practiced meditation unhealthily and was in a bad condition.
The bad spirits cannot disrupt the Buddha’s peace

At first, the Buddha-to-be lived a life of utmost luxury and wasn't able to practice the meditation necessary to enlightenment. Then, the Buddha-to-be realized this, and renounced all that could prevent him from the best meditation. Then, he travelled all over to find the path to enlightenment, and took up an extreme method of practice, nearly starving him to death. Finally, on a full moon day, he got donation of rice-milk soup that would power him to enlightenment, with the last good omen before he became the Buddha being the bowl travelling against the river when he placed it there.
A girl is offering the Buddha food
This appears to be showing the Buddha starting the meditation session where he becomes the Buddha, or this might be showing the Buddha feeling the bliss after freshly becoming the Buddha.
I can see the Buddha-to-very-soon-be in the last section of his deep meditation fighting mara's army and about to beat it.
After leaving the palace, he lived simply, without any luxuries, like servants and the same, soft bed he could sleep in.
This shows a woman donating a bowl of food that would end up nourishing the Buddha enough to become a Buddha.
He meets အဠာရandဉဒကရသေ့
It is known that they left him as they thought the Buddha-to-be was giving up on the practice since to their knowledge, only extreme practice led to enlightenment.
The enlightenment, then when the Bodhisattva became the Buddha, happened on the Kason full moon.
I can see the Buddha getting the donation of milk-rice, which then floated to the opposing side of the river after being placed there.

He lived in poverty and decided he would starve himself in extreme practice in hopes it would let him reach enlightenment then. It did not, as it was too extreme. His luxurious life back at the palace was also not enough.
The Buddha with wealth and happiness. He was provided with things he wanted at the palace.
I've seen this picture before, and can understand that it is a painting to represent the challenges in the final stretch before the Buddha became the Buddha.
The Buddha meditated under a Bodhi tree and gained enlightenment
He lived in extreme luxury and as an extremely wealthy man, safe from the suffering seen outside.
He met 2 teachers that taught him everything they knew, yet it wasn't enough to reach the level of enlightenment he sought after.
The Buddha fasted for several days while meditating
This shows the Buddha-to-be struggle as he eats little to nothing, while putting full concentration into meditating, which proved too extreme.
It was the daughter of a rich man, သုဇာတာ who gave the very powerful meal, at a great time too.

I know that there are extra rules to follow when one is a monk, and once in every eternity, a Buddha can come, but in order for that person to become a Buddha, many, many things must be done, and the soon-to-be-Buddha would have to keep the utmost attention in meditation.
